intent: The World Tsunami Awareness Day map: the Pacific's Ring of Fire drawn as the reveal, the 2004 Indian Ocean counter as the twist, Japan as the place hit most often, and the one rule — long quake, high ground — as the takeaway.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which ocean produces the MOST tsunamis?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which ocean produces the most tsunamis?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The Pacific. About 7 in 10 tsunamis on record start there, along the ring of quakes around its rim.

lines.direction: swing west to the Indian Ocean; the tag on 'Indian'; the Banda Aceh pin drops; from 'killed' a counter climbs to 230,000 — slowly, this is a toll, not a stat — a candle sticker beside it
lines.text: The deadliest, though, came from the Indian Ocean in 2004, and killed around 230,000 people.

lines.direction: push onto Japan; the tag on 'Japan'; the Sendai pin; on 'harbour' a TSU · NAMI split slides in — harbour on the left, wave on the right; the wave sticker on 'world'
lines.text: Japan is hit more often than anywhere; its own word, harbour wave, is what the world uses.

lines.direction: pull back out over the whole Pacific; the 5 NOV card on 'November'; the ring pulses again from 'lesson'; the mountain sticker lands on 'ground' and the siren sticker pulses
lines.text: The 5th of November is World Tsunami Awareness Day. The lesson: feel a long quake, head for high ground.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Long quake, high ground. Follow us.
